verdict.reasoning: REFUTED - no text is missing and no PDF-derived information is lost; the only difference is markdown nesting depth, which in this transcription carries no information from the source. Independently verified at 300 dpi. What the PDF actually prints (E:/Temp/specrecon/v683/spec_p683.png, printed page 653): after general rule 22 ('Identifier-4 is a receiving operand.') the page prints the bold clause heading '14.9.23.4 General rules', followed by general rules 1) and 2). What the markdown actually has: '' at line 28174 and '## 14.9.23.4 General rules' at line 28175 - the heading number and title are transcribed VERBATIM, and the anchor id is correct and stable. The claim's 'missing-heading' kind is a mislabel: nothing is missing. (The claim's line numbers are also all off by 3 - actual: 14.9.23 at 28053, .1 at 28056, .2 at 28061, .3 at 28086, .4 at 28175 - so the cited locations are a misquote, though the quoted strings themselves are right.) The substantive assertion - that .4 is '##' while .1/.2/.3 are '###' - IS factually true, but it is not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy, for three independently sufficient reasons: 1. The PDF encodes NO heading level. I rendered page 681 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v683b/spec_p681.png) to check the claim's premise. '14.9.23 INVOKE statement', '14.9.23.1 General', '14.9.23.2 General format' and '14.9.23.3 Syntax rules' are all set in the SAME bold serif face at the SAME size. The parent is typographically indistinguishable from its children. Hierarchy in the ISO standard is conveyed solely by the dotted clause NUMBER - and that number is transcribed exactly. So markdown '#' depth was never carrying anything the PDF said; the claim's premise ('printed in the same bold heading style as [its siblings]') is true but proves the opposite of what it is offered for. 2. Nothing is lost or ambiguous. Any reader or tool that sees '14.9.23.4 General rules' knows exactly where it sits; the anchor 'section-14-9-23-4' resolves cross-references correctly regardless of depth. Meaning is unchanged - the explicit rejection criterion for formatting-only differences applies. 3. It is a file-wide markdown convention inconsistency, not a page-683 event. specs/ISO_COBOL.md has 162 four-part-numbered headings at level 2 against 620 at level 3 (and 276 vs 508 for three-part), including the immediately preceding statement: 14.9.22.1/.2 are level 3 while 14.9.22.3 (line 27856) and 14.9.22.4 (27895) are level 2. The transcription's heading depth is not a coherent outline anywhere - the page-683 work unit shows the running header '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' at level 1 (above every real clause heading) and the page marker '## Page 683' at level 2, the same rank the claim objects to. Reporting one arbitrary instance of that as a page-683 PDF discrepancy is noise in a reconciliation ledger. Separately verified while on the page: the page-683 body is a faithful transcription - syntax rules 11 through 22 and general rules 1 and 2 all match the printed text, including the standard's own capitalization slip in rule 13 ('If Identifier-3, identifier-4, or identifier-5 ...').
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF/markdown discrepancy. The heading '14.9.23.4 General rules' is present in the markdown with its number and title transcribed verbatim (line 28175) and a correct anchor. The claim's real observation - '##' rather than '###' - is a markdown-outline inconsistency internal to the transcription: the ISO PDF sets 14.9.23 and 14.9.23.1/.2/.3 in identical bold type and encodes depth only in the dotted number, which is preserved. If wanted, the correct disposition is a single file-wide markdown-structure normalization task (162 four-part-numbered headings at level 2 vs 620 at level 3, plus the level-1 running header and level-2 page markers), not a per-page finding. The 'missing-heading' kind is wrong - nothing is missing - and the claim's line citations are each 3 lines low.
